units: <cite ref="Bava Kamma 119a:19">B. Kam. 119ᵃ</cite> <he>גבאי צדקה לוֹקְחִין וכ׳</he> collectors of charity may receive from them small contributions.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 3:13">Ex. R. s. 3</cite> <he>ל׳ את שלו</he> he received his due (punishment). Tanḥ. Korah 3 <he>ל׳ טליתו</he> he took up his cloak; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to carry away; to persuade. Ib. 1 (ref. to Num. XVI, 1) אין ויקח אלא משיכת וכ׳ vayikkaḥ means attraction by soft words; ib. 2 אין ויקח אלא לשון פליגה שלבו לְקָחוֹ vayikkaḥ has the meaning of separation, for his heart (pride) carried him away; Num. R. s. 18.

units: <cite ref="Mishnah Demai 4:5">Dem. IV, 5</cite> <he>קַח לי וכ׳</he> buy (provision) for me of one who is reliable &c.

<cite ref="Mishnah Demai 4:5">Ib.</cite> <he>הלך לִיקַּח … ולָקַחְתִּי לך וכ׳</he> if he went to buy of him (of the designated person), and … not finding him I bought of &c. Ib. V, 1 <he>הלוֹקֵחַ מן וכ׳</he> he who buys of a baker.
B. Mets. 16ᵇ לכשאֶקָּחֶנָּה when I shall have bought it; a. v. fr.—לוֹקֵחַ buyer.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 15b:19">Ib. 15ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>דמית ל׳</he> when the buyer is dead.

<cite ref="Berakhot 5a:8">Ber. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>ול׳ שמח</he> and the purchaser is glad; a. v. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="L00665"><he>לָקוּחַ</he></cite>, f. <he>לְקוּחָה</he>; pl. <he>לְקוּחִים</he>, <he>לְקוּחִון</he>; <cite ref="L00664"><he>לְקוּחוֹת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Pesachim 2:4:8">Y. Pes. II, 29ᵇ</cite> <he>הל׳ בכסף מעשר</he> that which has been bought with tithe-money.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 110a:6">B. Mets. 110ᵃ</cite> <he>ל׳ היא בידי</he> I have it as a purchased property.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 9:1:6">Y. Snh. IX, beg. 26ᵈ</cite> [read:] <he>עד שתהא הראשונה ל׳ לו</he> until the first wife has been legally acquired (betrothed) by him; (<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 11:1:5">Y. Yeb. XI, 11ᵈ</cite> top <cite ref="G00630"><he>זקוקה</he></cite>), v. <cite ref="L00685"><he>לְקִיחָה</he></cite>; a. fr.—V. <cite ref="L00664"><he>לְקוּחוֹת</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Maaser Sheni 1:3">Maas. Sh. I, 3</cite> <he>אינו נל׳ בכסף מעשר</he> must not be bought with tithe-money; <cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 1:7">Ḥull. I, 7</cite> <he>אינו ניקח</he>.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 2b">Kidd. 2ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 22:13">Deut. XXII, 13</cite>) it is not written <he>כי תִלָּקֵחַ אשה לאיש</he> if a woman is married (marries herself) to a man (Var. <he>תִקַּח</he>).

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12:1">Num. R. s. 12</cite>; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:11">Cant. R. to III, 11</cite>; Pesik. Vayhi, p. 4ᵃ (expl. <he>מִתְלַקַּחַת</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 9:24">Ex. IX, 24</cite>), v. <cite ref="P01516"><he>עֲשָׁשִׁיתָא</he></cite>.
